A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HadamRNN work. All 30 pages, including Appendices A–I, are available and readable; text and rendered-page comparisons support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original HadamRNN and Block-HadamRNN experiments in Section 4, additional benchmarks in Appendix F, and ablations and memory-retention experiments in Appendices G–H.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The architectures, matrix parameterizations, training procedure, and quantization methods are unchanged. Replacing b with b_i merely aligns two passages with the input bias already defined in Equation (1).

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the copy task, permuted and sequential MNIST, IMDB, SST-2, QQP, HAR-2, and DSA-19. The synthetic memory-perturbation scenario in Appendix G.2.2 is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each comparison: LSTM, ORNN, QORNN, and FastGRNN in Table 2; the same BERT variants in Table 6; and FastGRNN in Table 7.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, model sizes, bitwidths, training budgets, and testing procedures remain identical in Section 4 and Appendices D–I.

E4.justification: The training-stability analysis in Appendix E.2, linear-versus-ReLU ablation and memory-perturbation experiment in Appendix G, and row/column sign-switching ablation in Appendix H.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 retains five models trained with five different seeds for each bitwidth/learning-rate combination. Table 5 reports the same averages and standard deviations, with no additional uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including the appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains 94.88% pMNIST accuracy for HadamRNN with 4-bit U/V and unquantized activations; Table 6 retains 81.9% on SST-2 and 82.1% on QQP.

T1.justification: Definitions, propositions, proofs, and derivations are unchanged. Appendix G.2.1 replaces b with b_i inside the activation-derivative expression, matching Equation (8); this corrects notation without changing the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, efficiency, performance, and long-term-memory claims for binary and sparse ternary ORNNs.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning orthogonality, linear-unit memorization, sparsity tradeoffs, and column-sign switching are unchanged. The benchmark applicability boundaries and limitations in Section 4.1 and Appendix F are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, fixed-point instructions, and code-access information are identical. The input-bias clarification supplies no previously missing implementation detail.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the reference list are unchanged. No cited works or relationships to prior research are added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 changes 'the bias b' to 'the input bias b_i,' and Appendix G.2.1 makes the corresponding notation correction. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the remaining wording and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–10 retain identical displays, captions, and placement. Page organization is unchanged; the text corrections produce only incidental local wrapping and spacing.

improvement.justification: v4 slightly improves notational consistency in Section 3.2 and Appendix G.2.1, but v3 already identifies the same input bias in Equations (1) and (8) and Proposition H.1. These copyedits leave the methods, reasoning, evidence, and reproducibility information unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
